summary: The milestone completed 12 experiments in 45.4 minutes, including 8 compute-bound experiments. The longest compute-bound entries were the 40.84-minute exact-path adversarial capstone and evidence reconciliation and the 3.49-minute three-family GGUF load, CUDA admission, and lifecycle recovery. The timing data has no phase detail to explain their durations, and the locked compute-task GPU-idle classification is false.
bottlenecks_identified: Runtime was concentrated in the exact-path adversarial capstone and evidence reconciliation, but the timing data has no phase breakdown and therefore does not establish why it took 40.84 minutes.
Disk-modification-time reconstruction provides experiment-level duration but no task-linked phase or process telemetry.
The GPU snapshot is not linked to an experiment interval, so it cannot establish GPU efficiency across the compute-bound tasks.
The data has no simultaneous model-count or runner-selection receipt, so it cannot establish a missed DualGPURunner engagement.
improvements_suggested: Add task-scoped phase timers and checkpoints to capstone reconciliation so setup, verification, and evidence work can be measured and resumed independently.
Record experiment-linked GPU utilization, memory, process ownership, and cleanup receipts from task start through task end.
Record concurrent model count and selected runner; use DualGPURunner only when at least two models are loaded in parallel.
Cache unchanged evidence inputs and reconcile only changed evidence during exact-path capstones.
Schedule independent model work on an available GPU when task dependencies permit.
top_3_highest_leverage_actions: Instrument and checkpoint each capstone reconciliation phase.
Add task-linked GPU and process-lifecycle telemetry.
Add explicit model-count and runner-selection receipts with concurrency-aware GPU scheduling.
meta_reflection: The bounded data identifies where runtime accumulated but does not explain the internal cause or support a positive savings estimate. A single unlinked GPU snapshot also cannot prove inefficient compute execution or a missed concurrent-model dispatch.
